content.title: Data Analyst Onboarding Plan
content.summary: A structured onboarding plan for a Beginner Data Analyst in Business Intelligence, covering mandatory and optional learning items scheduled up to the first 30 days.

items.source_quote: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.
items.learning_objective: By the end of this module, the employee will be able to promptly acknowledge the employee handbook within 1 working day of joining and understand procedures if digital access is unavailable.
items.practical_activity: Simulate receiving the employee handbook digitally, then electronically acknowledge it within the 1-day timeframe. If digital access simulation fails, complete a supervised paper acknowledgement form.
items.lesson: Employees are required to acknowledge the current employee handbook within 1 working day of joining. This ensures awareness of company policies and procedures early in the employment relationship. If digital access to the handbook is unavailable for any reason, HR will document this outage and will arrange for the employee to provide a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same one-day period. This process keeps onboarding documentation compliant and ensures the employee is informed promptly.
checklist: Locate the digital employee handbook.
Complete electronic acknowledgement within 1 working day.
If digital access is unavailable, request supervised paper acknowledgement from HR.
Confirm HR records any access outages properly.

scenario.prompt: You joined the company today but encountered a system outage that prevents you from accessing the employee handbook online. What should you do to comply with company requirements?
scenario.expected_response: You notify HR about the access issue so they can record the outage and arrange for you to complete a supervised paper acknowledgement of the handbook within the same 1 working day.

quiz.question: What must an employee do if unable to access the employee handbook digitally upon joining?
options: Notify HR who records the outage and obtain supervised paper acknowledgement within 1 working day.
Delay handbook acknowledgement until access is restored.
Send an email to the manager requesting a handbook copy.
Do nothing and acknowledge once digital access is restored.
quiz.explanation: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.

rubric.criterion: Describes correct procedure when digital access is unavailable
Completes practical activity within 1 working day
Demonstrates understanding of acknowledgement timing and process

items.source_quote: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.
items.module_title: Handling Unexpected Absences Due to Emergencies
items.learning_objective: By module completion, the employee will understand the importance of timely notification of emergencies preventing attendance and the process for third-party notifications.
items.practical_activity: Role-play scenarios where you must inform your manager of an emergency preventing attendance. Also simulate a situation where you cannot communicate, and a nominated contact informs HR.
items.lesson: Employees must notify their manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents their attendance. This timely communication helps the organization manage work coverage and support. In cases where the employee cannot communicate personally, HR is authorized to accept notifications from a nominated contact who will provide details about the circumstances. HR will then record these circumstances to maintain accurate records of the absence.
checklist: Identify your direct manager’s contact information.
Notify your manager promptly if an emergency occurs preventing attendance.
If unable to notify, ensure a nominated contact informs HR.
Confirm HR records the circumstances accurately.

scenario.prompt: You suddenly fall ill and cannot attend work or contact your manager. What happens next according to company policy?
scenario.expected_response: HR accepts notification from a nominated contact about the emergency and records the circumstances since I am unable to communicate personally.

quiz.question: If you cannot personally notify your manager of an emergency absence, who does HR accept notification from?
options: A nominated contact designated by the employee
Any coworker
Your manager
A third-party vendor
quiz.explanation: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must notify the manager as soon as reasonably possible when an emergency prevents attendance. Where the employee cannot communicate, HR must accept notification from a nominated contact and record the circumstances.

rubric.criterion: Explains correct notification steps for emergency absences
Correctly identifies the role of HR and nominated contacts
Completes role-play notification and escalation accurately

items.source_quote: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.
items.learning_objective: Understand the importance and process of the manager's readiness review within the first 30 days, including documentation of gaps and follow-up planning.
items.practical_activity: Prepare a mock readiness review report identifying potential skill gaps, limits on supervised work, and setting follow-up review dates.
items.lesson: Managers are required to review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days of employment. This review assesses if the employee meets expected skills and knowledge. The manager documents any remaining learning gaps, defines limits on the employee’s supervised work, and sets dates for follow-up. This ensures structured development and supports the employee’s successful integration into their role.
checklist: Understand the criteria for employee readiness.
Work with your manager to discuss your progress before 30 days.
Help identify any gaps in your skillset or knowledge.
Assist in scheduling follow-up evaluations with your manager.

scenario.prompt: Your manager informs you that a readiness review will occur at the end of your first month. What will this review cover and why is it important?
scenario.expected_response: The review will cover any skill or knowledge gaps I may have, supervised work limitations, and set follow-up dates. It helps ensure I am progressing properly in my role and receiving needed support.

quiz.question: What must managers document during the employee readiness review?
options: Remaining gaps, supervised-work limits, and follow-up dates
Only completed training modules
Employee punctuality and attendance records
Employee salary and benefits
quiz.explanation: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.
quiz.evidence_quote: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes readiness review elements
Completes mock readiness review report comprehensively
Demonstrates understanding of follow-up importance

items.source_quote: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.
items.learning_objective: Learn to review archive searchability effectively and propose improvements to naming conventions or indexing to enhance data retrieval.
items.practical_activity: Conduct a simulated quarterly archive review, evaluate search effectiveness, and draft proposals for naming or indexing improvements.
items.lesson: Record owners are encouraged to review the searchability of archived records quarterly. This practice helps maintain efficient access to historical data. During each review, they assess how easy it is to locate records and propose improvements to naming or indexing schemes if necessary. These continuous improvements enhance the organization's data management and retrieval capabilities over time.
checklist: Schedule quarterly archive searchability reviews.
Evaluate current naming conventions and indexing effectiveness.
Identify possible improvements to naming or indexing.
Prepare proposals for suggested improvements.

scenario.prompt: During your quarterly archive review, you find difficulty retrieving certain records due to inconsistent naming. What should you do?
scenario.expected_response: I should propose improvements to the naming or indexing to make records easier to search and retrieve in the future.

quiz.question: What are record owners encouraged to do quarterly regarding archives?
options: Review archive searchability and propose improvements to naming or indexing
Delete old records to free up space
Ignore archives if not currently needed
Only catalog new records
quiz.explanation: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.
quiz.evidence_quote: Record owners are encouraged to review archive searchability quarterly and propose improvements to naming or indexing.

rubric.criterion: Identifies issues in archive searchability
Proposes viable naming or indexing improvements
Completes simulated archive review with actionable insights

items.source_quote: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.
items.learning_objective: Understand the importance of storing all operational evidence in the approved repository to ensure data integrity and compliance.
items.practical_activity: Simulate storing a sample operational decision document into the approved case repository and verify no local copies remain as the sole record.
items.lesson: Employees are required to keep all operational evidence in the designated case or document repository rather than only on local devices. This ensures that records of decisions or transactions are centrally accessible, secure, and compliant. Storing a local copy alone is insufficient and risks data loss or unauthorized access. Always use the approved system as the authoritative source for operational evidence.
checklist: Locate the approved case or document repository in the BI system.
Upload a test operational document to the repository.
Remove any local copies that could be the sole record.
Verify access and retrieval of the document from the repository.

scenario.prompt: You conducted an analysis resulting in an important decision report. How would you ensure compliance with company policy regarding record keeping?
scenario.expected_response: I would save the report directly to the approved case or document repository so it becomes the official record. I would also delete any local copies if they exist to avoid having a local copy as the sole record.

quiz.question: What is the correct procedure for storing operational evidence according to company policy?
options: Store all such evidence in the approved repository; local copies must not be the sole record.
Keep a local copy and optionally save it to the approved repository.
Only keep local copies as backups are handled separately.
Store evidence wherever convenient as long as you have a copy.
quiz.explanation: Company policy mandates that operational evidence must be stored in the approved case or document repository and that a local copy cannot be the sole record, ensuring data integrity and compliance.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.

rubric.criterion: Accurately stores evidence in approved repository
Ensures local copies are not sole record
Completes practical activity and checklist steps

items.source_quote: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.
items.learning_objective: Learn the steps for immediate response and reporting when an accidental data disclosure is detected.
items.practical_activity: Review a simulated accidental data disclosure scenario, identify actions to stop the transfer, preserve evidence, and complete a report following POL-09 procedures.
items.lesson: If you detect an unintended transfer or accidental disclosure of sensitive information, you must immediately act to halt the transfer if possible. Next, report the suspected disclosure as soon as possible via the official POL-09 incident reporting channel. Importantly, preserve all evidence related to the incident and do not conceal or delete any incident history to ensure transparency and proper resolution.
checklist: Identify signs of accidental data disclosure.
Attempt to stop the unintended transfer promptly.
Report the incident immediately through POL-09.
Preserve all related evidence without alteration or deletion.

scenario.prompt: You notice an email with sensitive data has been accidentally sent to an external party. What steps do you take?
scenario.expected_response: I would immediately try to stop or recall the email if possible and then report the suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. I would keep all evidence intact and not delete any incident records.

quiz.question: Which action is NOT consistent with company policy upon accidental data disclosure?
options: Concealing or silently deleting the incident history.
Stopping the unintended transfer when possible.
Reporting immediately through POL-09.
Preserving evidence related to the incident.
quiz.explanation: The policy clearly states employees must not conceal or silently delete the incident history. All other actions are required.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.

rubric.criterion: Acts promptly to stop data transfer
Follows correct reporting protocol via POL-09
Preserves incident evidence without deletion

items.source_quote: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.
items.learning_objective: Understand and apply respectful communication standards and appropriate reporting channels for workplace concerns.
items.practical_activity: Practice responding to workplace scenarios that involve potential harassment or discrimination, including how to report concerns confidentially through HR.
items.lesson: Maintaining respectful communication means never harassing, threatening, or discriminating against colleagues. If you witness behavior that concerns you, you must report it exclusively through the confidential HR channel. It is important not to circulate allegations among colleagues to protect privacy and avoid gossip or escalation. This approach promotes a safe, respectful workplace environment.
checklist: Familiarize with examples of respectful vs. inappropriate communication.
Always use polite, non-threatening language in work interactions.
Report any witnessed misconduct confidentially via HR channel.
Avoid discussing allegations with coworkers outside official channels.

scenario.prompt: You overhear a colleague making a discriminatory comment. What should you do?
scenario.expected_response: I should report my concern through the confidential HR channel immediately and avoid sharing the allegation with other colleagues to maintain confidentiality.

quiz.question: What is the correct way to handle witnessing harassment in the workplace?
options: Report concerns confidentially through HR and do not discuss with colleagues.
Discuss the issue openly with colleagues to raise awareness.
Ignore it if the behavior is not directed at you.
Confront the person publicly to stop the behavior.
quiz.explanation: The policy requires reporting concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.

rubric.criterion: Demonstrates understanding of respectful communication
Properly identifies confidential reporting procedures
Applies correct behavior in scenario and practical exercise

items.source_quote: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.
items.learning_objective: Achieve at least 80% on mandatory assessments and understand the retake procedure for incorrect attempts.
items.practical_activity: Complete a practice knowledge assessment quiz related to company policies, identify errors, and review relevant training materials before retaking the quiz if needed.
items.lesson: Employees must successfully score 80% or higher on all mandatory knowledge assessments to demonstrate understanding of company policies and procedures. If the first attempt fails, targeted revision of the relevant material is required before retaking the assessment. Importantly, the initial test score remains recorded for compliance tracking and cannot be erased or altered.
checklist: Complete the initial mandatory assessment.
Review all incorrect answers for revision.
Retake the assessment after targeted study if score is below 80%.
Ensure all attempts and scores are properly recorded.

scenario.prompt: You receive your knowledge assessment results and scored 75%. What should you do next?
scenario.expected_response: I must review the areas I missed carefully, complete targeted revision, and retake the assessment. The first failed score will remain recorded per policy.

quiz.question: What does the policy say about failing a mandatory knowledge assessment?
options: You must revise the relevant material and retake the assessment, original results remain recorded.
You can ignore the failed result if you retake later and pass.
The failed attempt is deleted after passing the retake.
Scores below 80% are acceptable if you pass overall.
quiz.explanation: The policy requires targeted revision and retaking on failure, with the original result remaining recorded.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.

rubric.criterion: Achieves required assessment score
Completes revision and retake if needed
Maintains transparency of all attempts

items.source_quote: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.
items.learning_objective: Understand the process and timeline for requesting attendance corrections and HR's role in record retention.
items.practical_activity: Simulate discovering an inaccurate attendance record and submit a correction request within the allowed timeframe.
items.lesson: Employees are required to promptly address any inaccurate attendance entries by requesting a correction. This must be done within 2 working days from the time the error is discovered to ensure timely and accurate attendance tracking. Meanwhile, HR is responsible for keeping the original attendance entry and all evidence supporting the correction to maintain record integrity and audit readiness. Timely action helps maintain accurate payroll and compliance with company policies.
checklist: Identify the inaccurate attendance entry promptly.
Submit a correction request within 2 working days of discovery.
Ensure the correction request includes supporting evidence.
Understand that HR retains original entries and evidence for auditing.

scenario.prompt: You notice your attendance entry shows you arrived at 9:30 AM, but you actually arrived at 9:00 AM two days ago. What should you do?
scenario.expected_response: You must submit a request to correct your attendance entry within 2 working days of noticing the error, including any evidence you have. HR will keep the original record and supporting information.

quiz.question: What is the maximum time allowed to request a correction for an inaccurate attendance entry?
options: 2 working days
1 calendar week
48 hours from the end of the workday
Immediately upon discovery
quiz.explanation: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.

rubric.criterion: Timely identification of attendance error
Completeness and accuracy of correction request
Adherence to simulation instructions in practical activity

items.source_quote: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.
items.learning_objective: Learn the requirements for document version linkage, change identification, and usage of correct versions for activities.
items.practical_activity: Review a document revision history and identify the linked previous version and the sections that changed. Use the correct document version for a simulated activity date.
items.lesson: Document management requires that each new revision be clearly linked to its previous version, and all changes must be identified to maintain clarity and traceability. Employees are required to use the document version that was effective on the date when their activity took place to ensure compliance and consistency. Historical versions are kept available for auditing purposes, so any discrepancies can be verified. Following these steps ensures accuracy and accountability in document handling.
checklist: Verify that each document revision links to the prior version.
Identify and document changed sections explicitly.
Use the document version effective on your activity date.
Understand that historical versions remain accessible for audits.

scenario.prompt: You are working with a policy document updated last month. How do you ensure you're using the correct version for your transaction dated two weeks ago?
scenario.expected_response: You must locate and use the version that was effective on the date of the activity, checking the revision links and changed sections as documented.

quiz.question: What must employees use when performing an activity on a specific date?
options: The document version effective on that date
The latest version of the document
Any version as long as it is approved
A draft version of the document
quiz.explanation: Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.
quiz.evidence_quote: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.

rubric.criterion: Correct identification of linked document versions
Accurate identification of changed sections
Appropriate use of document version in practical exercise

items.source_quote: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.
items.learning_objective: Understand roles and responsibilities in incident management including appointing an incident lead and task division.
items.practical_activity: Role-play appointing an incident lead and coordinating with IT to manage a simulated incident, ensuring clear role communication and documentation.
items.lesson: In incident management, the duty Operations Manager is responsible for appointing a single incident lead who will oversee the overall incident response coordination. The lead must be formally documented during handover to maintain clarity. While IT personnel handle technical containment measures, the incident lead manages business decisions and all related communications. This separation of responsibilities guarantees effective and timely handling of incidents, minimizes confusion, and ensures business continuity.
checklist: Identify the duty Operations Manager at incident start.
Appoint a single incident lead clearly and document the handover.
Coordinate with IT for technical containment.
Ensure the incident lead manages business decisions and communications.

scenario.prompt: During a system outage, who should be appointed to coordinate the business response and communications?
scenario.expected_response: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead who will coordinate business decisions and communications, while IT handles technical containment.

quiz.question: Who coordinates business decisions during an incident?
options: The incident lead appointed by the Operations Manager
The IT team lead
The HR department
All employees involved
quiz.explanation: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.
quiz.evidence_quote: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.

rubric.criterion: Clarity in describing incident lead appointment
Understanding separation of duties in scenario
Effective coordination demonstrated in role-play activity

items.source_quote: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.
items.learning_objective: Learn the timing and conditions for deleting temporary customer-data exports and understand preservation holds.
items.practical_activity: Simulate task completion and schedule deletion of exported customer data within 24 hours, respecting any preservation holds if indicated.
items.lesson: When temporary customer-data exports are approved for a task, they must be deleted within 24 elapsed hours after the task has concluded. This control prevents unnecessary data retention and protects customer privacy. However, if a preservation hold is documented, deletion is suspended, but only for the specific records identified in that hold. It is essential to strictly follow the deletion timeframe to comply with data governance policies and audits.
checklist: Identify when the approved task ends for the export.
Schedule deletion of the export within 24 elapsed hours afterward.
Check for any documented preservation hold on the records.
Suspend deletion only for records under preservation hold.

scenario.prompt: You completed a customer data export task yesterday. What is the deadline to delete the exported data?
scenario.expected_response: The exported data must be deleted within 24 elapsed hours after the task ended, unless a documented preservation hold exists for those records.

quiz.question: Within what timeframe must approved temporary customer-data exports be deleted after the task ends?
options: Within 24 elapsed hours
Within 48 working hours
Within 7 calendar days
Only when instructed by management
quiz.explanation: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.

rubric.criterion: Correct timing for deletion of data exports
Proper handling of preservation holds
Execution accuracy in simulated deletion task

items.source_quote: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.
items.module_title: Understanding Restricted Work and Prerequisite Training
items.learning_objective: By the end of this module, you will understand the necessity of completing prerequisite training before performing restricted tasks independently and recognize the limits of supervised practice approval.
items.practical_activity: Simulate a scenario where you identify a restricted task and a missing prerequisite. Prepare a request for supervised practice with a manager without marking the prerequisite complete.
items.lesson: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. It is important to recognize that a manager can arrange supervised practice, but under no circumstances should they mark an unmet prerequisite as complete. This ensures safety and adherence to company standards. Understanding and respecting this rule maintains work quality and compliance.
checklist: Review company policy on prerequisite trainings for restricted tasks.
Identify restricted tasks in your role that require prerequisite training.
Discuss supervised practice protocols with your manager.
Confirm prerequisites are officially completed before independent work.

scenario.prompt: You are assigned a restricted data analysis task but have not completed the prerequisite training. Your manager offers supervised practice but also suggests marking your prerequisite as complete. How do you respond?
scenario.expected_response: You explain that while supervised practice can be arranged, the prerequisite training must not be marked as complete until fully met, ensuring compliance with company policy.

quiz.question: What must be done before you can independently perform restricted tasks?
options: Complete the relevant prerequisite training.
Start supervised practice and mark the prerequisite complete.
Perform the task with a manager's verbal approval.
Wait one week before performing the task.
quiz.explanation: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks, and a manager must not mark an unmet prerequisite as complete.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.

rubric.criterion: Clearly explains the importance of prerequisite training and supervised practice limits in the scenario response.
Correctly identifies tasks requiring prerequisite training during practical activity.
Follows checklist steps thoroughly during the practical activity.

items.source_quote: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.
items.learning_objective: Understand how to properly assess parcel weight and route, recognize when to request assistance, and avoid assuming universal limits in manual handling.
items.practical_activity: Given several sample parcels with varying weights and routes, assess each and determine when to request approved handling assistance. Document your decisions with reasoning.
items.lesson: Employees must always assess the parcel weight and route before attempting to lift. If the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded, they must request approved handling assistance rather than acting alone. Importantly, employees must not invent a universal weight limit, as task assessments require specific consideration of each case. This ensures safety and prevents injury in manual handling tasks.
checklist: Examine posted safe-handling limits carefully before manual tasks.
Evaluate each parcel's weight and route individually.
Request approved handling assistance when limits are exceeded.
Never apply your own universal weight limit assumptions.

scenario.prompt: You face a heavy parcel that exceeds the posted safe-handling limit. A coworker suggests lifting it ourselves since it's 'not too heavy.' How do you respond?
scenario.expected_response: You explain that you must request approved handling assistance because the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded and refuse to invent a universal limit for safety.

quiz.question: What should you do if a parcel exceeds the posted safe-handling limit?
options: Request approved handling assistance.
Lift it carefully with a coworker.
Use your own judgment to decide if it's manageable.
Ignore the limit for small parcels.
quiz.explanation: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.

rubric.criterion: Appropriately requests assistance in the scenario response.
Accurately assesses parcel weight and route in the practical activity.
Follows checklist without inventing personal weight limits.

items.source_quote: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.
items.learning_objective: Be able to demonstrate all critical task steps to an authorized assessor, understanding that failing critical safety or privacy steps cannot be offset by score.
items.practical_activity: Perform a role-related task simulation, emphasizing critical safety and privacy steps while being evaluated by a peer acting as an authorized assessor.
items.lesson: Before performing work independently, employees must demonstrate the critical steps of their role task to an authorized assessor. Critical safety and privacy steps are essential, and failing these cannot be compensated by numerical scoring. This ensures all essential safeguards are met to protect company assets and personnel.
checklist: Identify critical safety and privacy steps in your tasks.
Practice these critical steps until proficient.
Schedule and participate in assessment with an authorized assessor.
Review feedback and address any critical step failures before independent work.

scenario.prompt: During your assessment, you fail a critical safety step but score well on other components. What is the outcome?
scenario.expected_response: You do not pass the assessment because a numerical score cannot compensate for failing a critical safety step and must address the failure before independent work.

quiz.question: If you fail a critical safety step during assessment, what happens?
options: You must retake the assessment regardless of your overall score.
Your good scores can compensate for it.
You can proceed with work but with caution.
You only need to practice that step further on the job.
quiz.explanation: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.

rubric.criterion: Clearly acknowledges the importance of critical steps in scenario response.
Performs all critical steps accurately during practical activity.
Follows checklist items thoroughly including assessment scheduling.

items.source_quote: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.
items.learning_objective: Be able to follow approved workflows for verifying requesters and understand the limits of information disclosure based on shipment number alone.
items.practical_activity: Review sample shipment requests and practice verifying requesters using the approved workflow, deciding which shipment details can be disclosed.
items.lesson: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing any shipment details. Simply having a shipment number does not authorize disclosure of recipient address or contact information. This policy protects privacy and ensures that sensitive data is shared only with authorized individuals.
checklist: Learn the approved verification workflow thoroughly.
Check requester credentials beyond shipment number only.
Disclose shipment details strictly per verification outcome.
Report any unauthorized disclosure attempts as per policy.

scenario.prompt: A requester provides a shipment number but no other verification details. They ask for the recipient's address. What do you do?
scenario.expected_response: You explain that you cannot disclose recipient address based solely on a shipment number and you need to verify the requester properly through the approved workflow before sharing any details.

quiz.question: Is a shipment number alone sufficient to disclose recipient address?
options: No, verification must follow the approved workflow.
Yes, the shipment number authorizes full disclosure.
Only if the requester is a colleague.
If approved by a manager afterward.
quiz.explanation: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.

rubric.criterion: Effectively refuses improper disclosure in the scenario response.
Properly verifies requesters using workflow in practical activity.
Adheres strictly to checklist steps on verification and disclosure.

items.source_quote: Employees are encouraged to discuss routine process frustrations privately with their manager and suggest a specific improvement supported by an example.
items.learning_objective: By the end of this module, the learner will be able to privately communicate routine process frustrations to their manager and propose specific improvements with clear examples.
items.practical_activity: Prepare and submit a written note to your manager describing a routine process frustration you have observed and suggest a specific improvement with an example.
items.lesson: This module encourages employees to openly but privately communicate routine frustrations related to work processes with their manager. When doing so, it is important to propose specific improvements backed by concrete examples. This approach fosters constructive dialogue and helps improve business processes. By discussing issues privately, you maintain professionalism and focus on solutions rather than just problems.
checklist: Identify a routine process frustration you have experienced or observed.
Write down the issue clearly and objectively.
Suggest a specific improvement to address the frustration.
Provide at least one example illustrating the issue and how your improvement would help.

scenario.prompt: You notice the data reconciliation process takes longer than expected due to manual steps that cause delays. How do you communicate this issue to your manager?

items.learning_objective: Understand documentation and review requirements before closing incidents, including recovery evidence, risks, corrective actions, and review timelines.

items.lesson: Before closing an incident, the incident lead must thoroughly document recovery evidence, any outstanding risks that remain, and identify the owners responsible for corrective actions. Following restoration, the Operations Manager has the obligation to review all critical incidents within 2 working days. This prompt review ensures timely assessment of incident impact and effectiveness of resolution steps, supporting continuous improvement in operational resilience.
checklist: Record all recovery evidence clearly.
List any outstanding risks associated with the incident.
Assign corrective action owners responsibly.
Schedule Operations Manager review within 2 working days after restoration.

items.source_quote: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.
items.learning_objective: Learn the order of precedence for workplace documents and how to resolve conflicts between them.
items.practical_activity: Given sample conflicting instructions from different document types, determine the correct authority to follow and practice escalating unresolved conflicts.
items.lesson: Employees must use the latest effective approved policy first, then follow the applicable Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), then an approved role guide, and lastly an FAQ. Check the applicable SOP and role guide documents.
Refer to FAQs only after the above documents are consulted.
Immediately escalate any unresolved conflicts to the policy owner.
Never ignore the document hierarchy when following instructions.

items.lesson: When a critical incident is discovered, employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes. Notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 minutes of discovery.
Begin the notification documentation as soon as practical after initial response.
Follow up until the incident is resolved or escalated further.

scenario.expected_response: I begin necessary emergency or containment actions immediately without waiting for a ticket, then notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 minutes, followed by documenting the notification as soon as practical.

quiz.question: Within what timeframe must you notify the Operations Manager after discovering a critical incident?

Within 1 hour
After completing emergency actions
At the end of your shift
quiz.explanation: Employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes of discovering a critical incident. Immediate emergency or containment actions must not wait for a ticket; the notification record must follow as soon as practical.
quiz.evidence_quote: Employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes of discovering a critical incident. Immediate emergency or containment actions must not wait for a ticket; the notification record must follow as soon as practical.

rubric.criterion: Starts emergency actions immediately in scenario response

Practices timely documentation and notification in practical activity

matrix_snapshot.title: Handbook acknowledgement
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must acknowledge the current handbook within 1 working day of joining. If access is unavailable, HR records the outage and obtains a supervised paper acknowledgement within the same period.

matrix_snapshot.title: Readiness review
matrix_snapshot.text: Managers must review employee readiness by the end of the first 30 calendar days and document remaining gaps, supervised-work limits and follow-up dates.

matrix_snapshot.title: Controlled repository
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must store operational evidence in the approved case or document repository. A local copy must not become the sole record of a decision or transaction.

matrix_snapshot.title: Accidental disclosure
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must stop an unintended transfer where possible and report suspected disclosure through POL-09 immediately. They must preserve evidence and must not conceal or silently delete the incident history.

matrix_snapshot.title: Respectful conduct
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must communicate respectfully and must not harass, threaten or discriminate against another person. A witness must report concerns through the confidential HR channel without circulating the allegation to colleagues.

matrix_snapshot.title: Knowledge assessment
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must score at least 80 percent on mandatory knowledge assessments. A failed attempt requires targeted revision and another attempt; the original result must remain recorded.

matrix_snapshot.title: Attendance correction
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must request correction of an inaccurate attendance entry within 2 working days of discovering it. HR must retain the original value and the evidence supporting correction.

matrix_snapshot.title: Version replacement
matrix_snapshot.text: Document owners must link each revision to the superseded version and identify changed sections. Employees must use the version effective on the date of the activity; historical copies remain available for audit.

matrix_snapshot.title: Single incident owner
matrix_snapshot.text: The duty Operations Manager must appoint an incident lead and record the handover. IT leads technical containment while the incident lead coordinates business decisions and communications.

matrix_snapshot.title: Temporary export removal
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must delete approved temporary customer-data exports within 24 elapsed hours after the approved task ends. A documented preservation hold suspends deletion only for the records identified in that hold.

matrix_snapshot.title: Restricted work
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must complete the relevant prerequisite training before independently performing restricted tasks. A manager may arrange supervised practice but must not mark an unmet prerequisite complete.

matrix_snapshot.title: Manual handling
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must assess parcel weight and route before lifting and must request approved handling assistance when the posted safe-handling limit is exceeded. They must not invent a universal weight limit where a task assessment is required.

matrix_snapshot.title: Practical competence
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must demonstrate the critical steps of a role task to an authorized assessor before independent work. A numerical score cannot compensate for a failed safety or privacy critical step.

matrix_snapshot.title: Recipient verification
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must verify the requester using the approved workflow before disclosing shipment details. A shipment number alone does not authorize disclosure of the recipient address or contact details.

matrix_snapshot.title: Constructive feedback
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees are encouraged to discuss routine process frustrations privately with their manager and suggest a specific improvement supported by an example.

matrix_snapshot.title: Controlled copies
matrix_snapshot.text: Document owners must record document ID, owner, version, approval role and effective date before release. An unapproved draft must not be used to assign mandatory training.

matrix_snapshot.title: Approve analysis purpose
matrix_snapshot.text: The Data Analyst must document the business question, requested fields and intended recipients before receiving restricted data. The Operations Manager must approve the scope.

matrix_snapshot.title: Approved fallback
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must use only the approved numbered fallback forms or controlled offline register during an outage. Personal notebooks and unapproved messaging groups must not hold customer records.

matrix_snapshot.title: Dispose of extracts
matrix_snapshot.text: The Data Analyst must register temporary customer-data extracts and delete them within POL-06 limits unless an identified preservation hold applies.

matrix_snapshot.title: Suspicious content
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must report suspicious links, attachments or unexpected authentication requests to IT without opening them. If already opened, the employee must report the action and follow the incident process in POL-09.

matrix_snapshot.title: Screen lock
matrix_snapshot.text: Employees must lock an unattended workstation immediately and configure automatic locking after no more than 5 minutes of inactivity. Shared warehouse terminals follow the same limit.

matrix_snapshot.title: Continuity activation
matrix_snapshot.text: Only the duty Operations Manager may activate the continuity procedure after assessing service impact. If immediate danger exists, employees must take the safety actions in POL-08 without waiting for activation.

matrix_snapshot.title: Planned absence notice

matrix_snapshot.title: Non retaliation

requirements.text: Employees must use only the approved numbered fallback forms or controlled offline register during an outage. Personal notebooks and unapproved messaging groups must not hold customer records.
requirements.title: Approved fallback

requirements.text: The Data Analyst must register temporary customer-data extracts and delete them within POL-06 limits unless an identified preservation hold applies.
requirements.title: Dispose of extracts

requirements.text: Employees must report suspicious links, attachments or unexpected authentication requests to IT without opening them. If already opened, the employee must report the action and follow the incident process in POL-09.
requirements.title: Suspicious content

requirements.text: Employees must lock an unattended workstation immediately and configure automatic locking after no more than 5 minutes of inactivity. Shared warehouse terminals follow the same limit.
requirements.title: Screen lock

requirements.text: Only the duty Operations Manager may activate the continuity procedure after assessing service impact. If immediate danger exists, employees must take the safety actions in POL-08 without waiting for activation.
requirements.title: Continuity activation

requirements.text: Employees must submit a planned absence request at least 3 working days before the proposed start. The manager may approve shorter notice only after recording a coverage arrangement.
requirements.title: Planned absence notice

requirements.text: Managers must not disadvantage a person for raising a good-faith concern or participating in an investigation. Any alleged retaliation must be referred to the Managing Director.
requirements.title: Non retaliation

requirements.text: Employees must stop work and use the signed evacuation route when the alarm sounds. They must report to the assembly point and must not re-enter until the incident lead authorizes it.
requirements.title: Emergency evacuation

requirements.text: Employees hosting a visitor must arrange registration, a visible visitor pass and an escort in restricted areas. Visitors must not use employee access credentials.
requirements.title: Visitor escort

requirements.text: Employees must log access, correction or deletion requests and refer them to the Operations Manager on the same working day. Employees must not promise deletion before checking preservation requirements.
requirements.title: Privacy requests

requirements.text: Employees must record only shipment ID, action, time and assigned operator in the fallback register. Additional personal data requires explicit incident-lead approval and privacy controls.
requirements.title: Minimum fallback data

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to complete optional phishing simulations and discuss the warning signs with IT after the exercise.
requirements.title: Security practice

requirements.text: Employees must not operate powered warehouse equipment without documented authorization and task-specific training. Observing another operator does not grant authorization.
requirements.title: Restricted equipment

requirements.text: HR must retain onboarding acknowledgements, assessment attempts and readiness decisions for 24 months after the employee leaves the company, unless a preservation hold applies.
requirements.title: Training retention

requirements.text: The Data Analyst must document numerator, denominator, time window and exclusions for each published performance measure. A zero denominator must be shown as not applicable rather than a fabricated percentage.
requirements.title: Define measures

requirements.text: Employees must use company-managed devices or an explicitly approved device profile to access restricted data. Personal storage services must not receive company files.
requirements.title: Approved devices

requirements.text: Employees must transfer open tasks, critical deadlines and escalation contacts to the designated cover before planned absence. Customer personal data must remain in approved systems.
requirements.title: Shift handover

requirements.text: Employees may propose a simpler fallback step after a rehearsal, provided the proposal preserves privacy, traceability and independent approval.
requirements.title: Continuity improvements

requirements.text: Employees must declare any offered gift valued above PKR 1,000 to HR before accepting it. Cash and cash-equivalent gifts are prohibited at any value; splitting a gift does not avoid this rule.
requirements.title: Gift declaration

requirements.text: Assigned record owners must reconcile fallback entries within 1 working day of restoration, resolve mismatches and dispose of temporary copies according to POL-06 and POL-07.
requirements.title: Fallback reconciliation

requirements.text: Employees must use fictional or irreversibly anonymized customer examples in training and demonstrations. Replacing a name alone does not anonymize a record containing a real telephone number or address.
requirements.title: Training data

requirements.text: Employees must obtain Managing Director approval before representing the company publicly or publishing customer-related material. Personal accounts must not disclose internal records.
requirements.title: Public statements

requirements.text: Employees must record actual events and must not fabricate delivery attempts, training completion, assessment results or approvals. Corrections must retain the original entry and the reason for amendment.
requirements.title: Accurate records

requirements.text: Responders must preserve relevant logs, messages and event identifiers without modifying originals. Evidence access must be restricted to the response team and a preservation hold applied where necessary.
requirements.title: Evidence preservation

requirements.text: Employees must use the confidential HR channel to report misconduct. If the concern involves HR, the report must go directly to the Managing Director.
requirements.title: Confidential reporting

requirements.text: Employees must obtain recorded approval before taking planned leave. Submission alone is not approval, and employees must not approve their own request.
requirements.title: Approval before absence

requirements.text: Employees may select an optional development topic after agreeing the time allocation with their manager; optional learning must not delay mandatory training.
requirements.title: Personal development

requirements.text: Employees must transfer personal data only through approved company systems to authorized recipients. Personal messaging accounts and publicly accessible links are prohibited.
requirements.title: Approved transfer

requirements.text: Record owners must retain routine delivery-event records for 180 calendar days after case closure. A documented preservation hold overrides routine deletion until the hold is formally released.
requirements.title: Routine operational retention

requirements.text: Employees must refer records with no applicable retention category to the Operations Manager before deletion. They must not infer a deadline from an unrelated record type.
requirements.title: Retention uncertainty

requirements.text: Teams are encouraged to rehearse one incident scenario each month and document a specific improvement to the response procedure.
requirements.title: Response rehearsal

requirements.text: HR must assign an onboarding plan based on role, experience, location and applicable requirements. Prior experience may change practice difficulty but must not remove mandatory acknowledgements.
requirements.title: Individual plan

requirements.text: Employees must access and collect only the customer fields needed for an assigned task. Full identity documents must not be requested for routine parcel tracking.
requirements.title: Minimum necessary data

requirements.text: The first available responder must create an incident record containing observed facts, discovery time, affected services and initial actions. Speculation must be labelled and credentials must be excluded.
requirements.title: Incident record

requirements.text: During an activated continuity event, the incident lead must issue an internal status checkpoint at least every 30 elapsed minutes until normal service resumes. A checkpoint must state current impact, owner and next update time.
requirements.title: Outage checkpoints

requirements.text: The Data Analyst must use approved source datasets and record their extraction time and version. An unverified spreadsheet must not silently replace an authoritative dataset.
requirements.title: Use approved sources

requirements.text: Record owners must correct errors through an auditable amendment recording author, time and reason. Original transaction values must not be overwritten without history.
requirements.title: Record correction

requirements.text: The Data Analyst must remove direct identifiers unless the approved question requires them. Group-level reporting must suppress cells containing fewer than 5 individuals or shipments where re-identification is plausible.
requirements.title: Minimize identifiers

requirements.text: Employees must pause the affected activity and ask the document owner when two equally authoritative instructions conflict or a necessary limit is missing. The owner must record the resolution before work resumes.
requirements.title: Unclear requirements

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to discuss anticipated leave early so teams can plan coverage before a formal request is submitted.
requirements.title: Calendar planning

requirements.text: Managers must confirm required operational coverage before approving concurrent absences. If coverage cannot be arranged, the manager must record the reason and discuss alternative dates.
requirements.title: Minimum coverage

requirements.text: Employees must activate multifactor authentication before accessing email, remote access or systems holding customer records. IT must provide an approved recovery method rather than disabling the requirement.
requirements.title: Multifactor authentication

requirements.text: Record owners must use approved disposal methods and retain a disposal log identifying category, date range, authorization and completion date. Disposal must not expose readable personal data.
requirements.title: Secure disposal

requirements.text: Employees must disclose a personal or financial relationship with a merchant or supplier before participating in its selection, payment or complaint decision. The manager must assign an independent decision-maker.
requirements.title: Personal interests

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to suggest improvements to workstation layout or parcel movement after discussing them with the supervisor.
requirements.title: Safety suggestions

requirements.text: The Data Analyst must check missing identifiers, duplicate events and inconsistent timestamps before publication. Material limitations must appear with the report.
requirements.title: Validate data quality

requirements.text: Reviewers must verify required evidence before recording completion. Reading a module alone does not demonstrate practical competence or substitute for a required policy acknowledgement.
requirements.title: Completion integrity

requirements.text: Employees must record near misses even when no injury or damage occurs. The supervisor must assign a corrective action owner and verify completion.
requirements.title: Near misses

requirements.text: The Data Analyst may explore additional aggregate measures in a clearly labelled experimental report that is not used for operational decisions before review.
requirements.title: Explore improvements

requirements.text: HR must record each employee role, department, joining date and reporting manager before assigning onboarding. A temporary role change requires a recorded start date, end date and additional requirements.
requirements.title: Role assignment

requirements.text: The Data Analyst must obtain owner review before publishing a report used for merchant or employee decisions. Review must cover interpretation, privacy and data quality.
requirements.title: Review publication

requirements.text: The incident lead must obtain an IT health check and an operational sample check before declaring normal service restored. A login screen alone is not evidence of end-to-end recovery.
requirements.title: Recovery verification

requirements.text: Employees must obtain IT approval before installing software or browser extensions on company devices. IT must verify business purpose and permitted access before approval.
requirements.title: Software installation

requirements.text: Employees entering marked warehouse handling zones must wear the posted protective equipment. The supervisor must stop the task if suitable equipment is unavailable.
requirements.title: Personal protective equipment

requirements.text: Employees must store API keys and service credentials only in approved secret storage and must not include them in source repositories, screenshots, training examples or support tickets.
requirements.title: Secrets handling

requirements.text: Only the incident lead or a designated spokesperson may issue incident updates to merchants or customers. Updates must distinguish confirmed impact from investigation assumptions.
requirements.title: External communication

requirements.text: Employees may suggest removal of unnecessary personal-data fields from forms, reports or dashboards to the relevant process owner.
requirements.title: Privacy improvements

requirements.text: Employees must classify an incident as critical when it involves immediate physical danger, suspected exposure of customer data or complete loss of dispatch capability. Where severity is uncertain, they must escalate as critical pending review.
requirements.title: Severity classification

requirements.text: Employees must check shipment and transaction identifiers before entering recovered work into the restored system. Potential duplicates must be held for review rather than posted again.
requirements.title: Duplicate prevention

requirements.text: Training managers must distribute learning across Day 1, Week 1, Week 2 and First 30 Days. Mandatory operational deadlines and prerequisites take priority over a convenient stage label.
requirements.title: Learning stages

requirements.text: Employees must report a non-urgent safety concern before the end of the current shift. An immediate danger requires stopping the activity and alerting the shift supervisor at once.
requirements.title: Safety concern reporting

requirements.text: HR must restrict medical or other sensitive absence details to authorized People Operations staff. Operational managers receive only information needed to arrange work.
requirements.title: Sensitive absence details

requirements.text: The Operations Manager must identify scope, owner and start date when issuing a preservation hold. Record owners must suspend scheduled deletion for the named records until written release.
requirements.title: Preservation holds

requirements.text: Employees are encouraged to arrange a weekly discussion with an experienced colleague during the first month to clarify workflows and identify useful practice.
requirements.title: Onboarding buddy

requirements.text: The incident lead must record recovery evidence, outstanding risks and corrective action owners before closure. The Operations Manager must review critical incidents within 2 working days after restoration.
requirements.title: Incident closure

requirements.text: Employees must use individually assigned accounts and must not share passwords or authentication codes. Service accounts require a named IT owner and must not be used for routine interactive work.
requirements.title: Individual accounts

requirements.text: Employees must follow the latest effective approved policy, then the applicable SOP, then an approved role guide, then an FAQ. A lower-authority document cannot override a policy; unresolved conflicts go to the policy owner before action.
requirements.title: Authoritative instructions

requirements.text: Employees must notify the duty Operations Manager within 15 elapsed minutes of discovering a critical incident. Immediate emergency or containment actions must not wait for a ticket; the notification record must follow as soon as practical.
requirements.title: Critical escalation

requirements.text: Employees must complete core orientation within 2 working days of joining. HR must schedule a replacement session within that deadline if the original session is cancelled.
requirements.title: Core orientation
